findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted and wrong-offset grant check
findings.body: The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches, so the matcher rejects correct IDs and accepts wrong ones. The offset is also wrong: the format is `onrtac:`, so the grant shortcut is at chars 4-6, i.e. substring(4, 6). Substring(3,5) reads the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant. As written the matcher can never match a correct ID (it would be 'tac' vs 'ac'), so any test using expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and similar would fail, or pass only by accident. It should be `!substring(4,6).equals(expected)` and the comment should say chars 5-6.

findings.title: Null check on rawTokenId validates grantType instead
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks grantType a second time, so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and later encoded as the string "null" in the token ID. It should check rawTokenId.

findings.title: initToken throws if grant type attribute not set
findings.body: initToken now calls encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException if the grant type is unknown ("na" is a valid value in the shortcut map, but a null attribute becomes UNKNOWN and then encodes as 'na'). Even so, several paths create access tokens without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE (implicit/hybrid flows, other callers of createClientAccessToken, and any token created before the attribute is set). Those produce 'na' IDs silently, which defeats the feature. A custom or unregistered grant would fail token creation outright. Related: the getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) call relies on session.getContext().getClient() being non-null, which may NPE in some flows.

findings.title: Duplicate shortcut validation is weak
findings.body: Duplicates are detected only by comparing map sizes after puts that overwrite silently. If two grants share a shortcut, the later one overwrites the earlier in grantsByShortcuts, so the sizes differ only by accident. The lazy refresh paths also never validate. Collisions should be checked explicitly on each put. Also, a shortcut of 'na' from a grant would collide with UNKNOWN.
